blocks.content: The primary objective of FCI is to safeguard the interests of farmers through remunerative price support while ensuring national food security via efficient distribution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Food Corporation of India (FCI) was established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 to fulfill the objectives of the National Food Policy.
Provides effective price support operations at Minimum Support Price (MSP) to safeguard the financial interests of farmers.
Facilitates national distribution of essential foodgrains through the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS).
Maintains minimum operational and strategic buffer stocks to ensure continuous national food security.
Intervenes in the market via Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) to stabilize prices of food commodities.

rows: Meets regular monthly distribution demands under TPDS and welfare schemes
Serves as a reserve against crop failures, emergency shortages, and price spikes
Fluctuates according to seasonal harvest and monthly allocation cycles
Maintained at prescribed minimum statutory threshold levels throughout the year

items: FCI is a statutory body created under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 (Act No. 37 of 1964).
Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by CACP, but FCI acts as the primary agency executing price support procurement.
Quarterly buffer stock norms (1st Jan, 1st April, 1st July, 1st Oct) are set by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
